artifacts.notes: The press route https://press.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decl_19651028_nostra-aetate_en.html and content-delivery route https://www.vatican.va/content/dam/wss/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decl_19651028_nostra-aetate_en.html returned byte-identical 17231-byte responses with this SHA-256 on 2026-07-24; the aliases are not duplicated. The response contains the complete numbered English body and consolidated notes but no promulgation or subscription block. Delivered defects include article 3's «all- powerful»; article 4's broken punctuation in «Christ-Abraham's sons according to faith (6)-are», «Gentiles. making», and «calls He issues-such»; and note 5's presentation of Gregory VII's Epistola III, 21 as «letter XXI» with only the imprecise «Pl. 148, col. 450f.» citation. This list records known source-local defects without claiming an exhaustive diplomatic collation. Exact bytes are identified but not retained.

passages.context: The complete English article was inspected for the Declaration's recognition of what is true and holy in other religions, its insistence on Christ as the way, truth, and life in whom the fullness of religious life is found, and its call to prudent, loving dialogue and collaboration joined to Christian witness.
passages.notes: The article's recognition and dialogue language is not evidence for parallel saving religions or for suppressing its Christological qualification. Its source note 4 is visible but does not make a consumer an independent user of 2 Corinthians 5:18-19.

passages.context: The complete English article was inspected for the Church's spiritual bond with the Jewish people, the non-imputation of Christ's Passion to all Jews then or now, the rejection of presenting Jews as rejected or accursed by God, and the denunciation of hatred, persecution, and antisemitism.
passages.notes: The dated English delivery contains several punctuation defects recorded at artifact level; the Latin web and Acta witnesses control their identification. passages.context: The complete English article was inspected for the relation between love of God and fraternal conduct, the rejection of theories or practices that impair human dignity and its consequent rights, and the Church's rejection of discrimination or harassment based on race, color, condition of life, or religion.
passages.notes: The article supplies a conciliar doctrinal and moral boundary, not a complete account of current civil law, jurisdiction-specific legal remedies, or every later magisterial treatment of discrimination.

work.author: Second Vatican Council
work.description: The Second Vatican Council's Declaration on the Relation of the Church to Non-Christian Religions, solemnly promulgated by Pope Paul VI on 28 October 1965. Its numbered articles 1-5 address humanity's common origin and end, the Church's relation to non-Christian religions, Muslims, the Jewish people, antisemitism, and discrimination.
